PullRequest.Title: Show per-turn file changes summary for agent host chat responses
PullRequest.Body:
Fix #318891

## What

Renders the collapsible **"Changed N files"** summary under completed **agent host** chat responses when `chat.checkpoints.showFileChanges` is enabled. Until now this summary only appeared for regular local chat sessions; agent host responses skipped it.

The summary is driven by the **per-turn changeset** the agent host computes server-side — the same authoritative source backing the Agents window Changes view — rather than the chat editing session. This means it reflects all of a turn's changes (including edits made via terminal/external tools), not just the ones tracked through chat's own edit pipeline.

## How

- **`IChatResponseFileChangesService`** (new): a small per-session-type provider registry. `ChatCheckpointFileChangesSummaryContentPart` consults it first and falls back to the chat editing session for non-agent-host sessions, so local chat is unchanged. The summary part now **self-hides** when its resolved diffs are empty, so a turn that made no edits shows nothing.
- **`AgentHostResponseFileChangesProvider`** (new): for a given response it subscribes to the session's per-turn changeset (keyed by the response's turn id), gated on the agent advertising a `turn` changeset, and maps the changeset files into edit-session diffs. Subscriptions are lazy and memoized per request.
- **Renderer gate**: `getChatFileChangesSummaryPart` now creates the summary part for agent host responses (which emit external edits rather than text/notebook edit groups); the existing gate is unchanged for other sessions.
- **Shared `normalizeFileEdit` helper**: extracts the create/delete/rename/edit detection and URI parsing that was duplicated across the external-edit, snapshot, and changeset mappers.

## Testing

- Unit tests for the `normalizeFileEdit` helper (all four file statuses) and the agent host provider (mapping, empty-when-no-turn-changeset, memoization).
- Existing snapshot-controller, state-adapter, and sessions-provider suites still pass after the refactor.
- Manual smoke test against a real Copilot agent host session: the summary renders with correct file list and +/- counts; the modified-file diff resolves before-content correctly in the editor window; a no-edit turn shows no summary.

### Known v1 caveat

For **created** files there is no before-content, so opening that file's diff shows no delta (the summary's +/- counts are still correct since they come from the server). The same class of edge case applies to deletions.

(Written by Copilot)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Ownership and cleanup paths are explicit: the map has a single set site and no delete/clear, while its provider outlives individual rows and chat sessions. Only the exact heap size per turn is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Map keys and per-turn observable/closure graphs
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retained entries grow once per distinct backend-session/request pair whose response summary is rendered, across all agent chats visited during the handler's lifetime.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Steadily increasing retained heap and associated GC scanning in long-lived windows that browse many agent turns.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no handler-wide per-request provider cache for agent-host response summaries.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each first lookup inserts a per-turn observable into `_perRequest`, but no code removes that entry when the row is unmounted or when `AgentHostChatSession` disposal releases the backend session.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 55 newly stores each request observable in a handler-lifetime map with no corresponding delete path.
Findings.Title: Evict memoized turn observables after their summaries are released
Findings.Impact: With file-change summaries enabled, opening and scrolling through many agent chats permanently retains one observable graph and composite URI/request key per visited turn until the agent registration or workbench is disposed.
Findings.Evidence: The new `_perRequest` map is owned by `AgentHostResponseFileChangesProvider`, which is registered once on the long-lived `AgentHostSessionHandler`. Line 55 inserts every distinct key. Renderer disposal removes observers, and `Derived.onLastObserverRemoved` clears subscription/value caches, but it does not remove the outer map entry. `AgentHostSessionHandler`'s per-chat dispose callback releases active session subscriptions without notifying this provider, so closed sessions' entries remain reachable.
Findings.Recommendation: Remove this permanent memoization (the connection already refcounts/coalesces live subscriptions), or add observer/session-lifecycle eviction so an inactive or closed session's request entries are deleted.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added gate, constructor call, and unconditional WorkbenchList construction are directly traced. The exact frame-time cost varies with viewport and hardware, but the mechanism and repetition for no-edit mounted rows are explicit.
Findings.PerformanceResource: WorkbenchList instances, scoped context keys, DOM nodes, listeners, and observable/list allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The synchronous construction repeats for every mounted completed agent-host response and again as responses are recreated while scrolling; no-edit turns pay the same setup cost as turns with files.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Extra main-thread rendering work and allocation/GC pressure can make opening or scrolling no-edit-heavy agent chats janky.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this gate changed, agent-host responses did not pass the text/notebook edit-group check, so they did not construct a changes-summary content part or its nested WorkbenchList.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new agent-host exemption appends a changesSummary part to every completed agent-host response whenever the setting is enabled, even though the asynchronous provider commonly resolves to an empty array.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1502 bypasses the prior edit-group gate for agent-host sessions, newly routing responses with no file changes into the heavyweight summary constructor.
Findings.Title: Defer the nested file list until changes resolve non-empty
Findings.Impact: With `chat.checkpoints.showFileChanges` enabled, opening or scrolling a conversation containing many short/no-edit turns synchronously constructs a full hidden nested list for each mounted response before the provider establishes that there are no files.
Findings.Evidence: This added condition admits all completed agent-host responses. `renderChangesSummary` then constructs `ChatCheckpointFileChangesSummaryContentPart`; its constructor unconditionally calls both `renderHeader` and `renderFilesList`, and `renderFilesList` immediately creates a `WorkbenchList`. The newly added autorun merely applies `display:none` after reading empty diffs, so it does not avoid that list construction. `WorkbenchList` itself creates scoped context keys, registers with the list service, and installs listeners, establishing substantial synchronous UI work rather than a metadata-only pass.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep observing the provider with a lightweight placeholder, but create the header and WorkbenchList only after the first non-empty diff array; empty turns should dispose without ever constructing nested list infrastructure.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and scroll completed agent-host responses with file-change summaries enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Chat row rendering synchronously constructs the summary DOM and nested WorkbenchList before the asynchronous changeset is known; the base response can render before remote state arrives, but summary visibility/counts depend on the turn changeset subscription.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical shared resource per backend session; existing handler/session references cause the connection manager to coalesce additional mounted-row references.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agent-host chat summaries were skipped, so this render path did not acquire summary-owned references.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Needed to discover turn-changeset support, but normally reuses the already-active session subscription; it does not block base response rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to a per-turn changeset state resource
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One distinct subscription per mounted cold turn; no-edit turns still require the subscription to resolve empty.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No per-response changeset subscription was made by the chat renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the base chat-response critical path but required before the summary can show or self-hide authoritatively.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Mounted completed responses in the viewport and distinct turns encountered while scrolling; no-edit turns have the same initial UI construction as edited turns.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All mounted summary observables may acquire subscriptions concurrently. The subscription manager refcounts/coalesces the shared session URI, while each distinct turn changeset URI is independent and has no shared limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The provider memoizes observables by backend session plus request ID. Concurrent/repeated lookup for one turn shares that observable; cold turns acquire changeset state, and unobserved derived observables release subscription/value caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new gate admits every completed agent-host response and the content-part constructor unconditionally builds the nested list before empty diffs hide it.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of simultaneously mounted rows and milliseconds spent constructing each WorkbenchList vary by viewport, response height, and hardware; the eager construction for every no-edit row is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager rendering regression: defer heavyweight nested-list construction until diffs are non-empty.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, scroll through, and close many agent-host chat histories in one workbench lifetime
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Per-turn observable lookup occurs during row construction; retention is not on a single interaction's critical path but accumulates after rows and chat models are disposed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire and later release session and per-turn state subscriptions while a summary is observed
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one refcounted wire subscription per active resource, with distinct turn URIs; released after row disposal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No response-summary subscriptions or per-turn memoization existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The boundary is active only while observed and is not itself leaked; the reported regression is the handler-lifetime JavaScript cache entry left after release.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total distinct backend-session/request pairs ever rendered while the handler remains registered, including turns from closed sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Subscriptions are refcounted and released when the last row observer is removed; the retained outer map entries remain regardless of active concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Positive memoization has no eviction, session-lifecycle invalidation, or size bound. Derived observables clear their cached value and dependencies when unobserved, but the map retains each key and observable/closure graph.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: `_perRequest` has insertion but no delete/clear and its provider outlives individual chat sessions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Heap bytes per inactive turn are modest and derived values are cleared, but total retained entries is unbounded and depends on how many histories a long-lived window visits.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cache-lifecycle regression: evict inactive/session-owned entries or avoid permanent memoization.

Scenarios.Scenario: Map protocol file edits into external edits, session changes, and response diff rows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Synchronous URI parsing and file-kind classification runs when protocol state/tool-call data is adapted for display.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of changed files in a tool call or changeset; one normalization pass per file.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Pure synchronous per-file mapping with no queue, limiter, or asynchronous fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used or needed; parsed URI objects live with the mapped result.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all normalizeFileEdit callers and changed mappings were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: File counts vary, but the refactor performs comparable URI parsing to the duplicated prior implementations and introduces no heavyweight boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the shared helper preserves linear per-file work and does not add I/O or retained state.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 13 changed files. Reported eager hidden nested-list construction for no-edit agent turns and the unbounded handler-lifetime per-request observable cache; remote subscription fan-out and URI normalization were traced and did not yield additional findings.
